name: Bachelor of Fisheries Science (B.F.Sc.)
duration_note: Includes 3 years of classroom, hatchery, and laboratory training followed by a full final year under ICAR's Student READY framework, comprising Rural Fisheries Work Experience (RFWE), hands-on experiential aquaculture enterprise modules, and in-plant seafood industrial training.

hero.summary: A four-year professional degree covering commercial aquaculture, marine biology, fish breeding, disease diagnostics, seafood processing, fishing vessel technology, and aquatic resource conservation under the ICAR Deans Committee curriculum.

overview.heading: What the Bachelor of Fisheries Science (B.F.Sc.) covers
paragraphs: Bachelor of Fisheries Science (B.F.Sc.) is a professional four-year undergraduate degree designed to prepare qualified specialists for India's blue economy. Developed under the guidelines of the ICAR Deans Committee, the programme addresses the scientific management of inland, brackishwater, and marine fisheries resources.

The curriculum integrates seven core academic divisions: Aquaculture (breeding and farming of carps, catfishes, shrimps, crabs, and seaweeds), Fisheries Resource Management (taxonomy, population dynamics, fish biology, and marine ecology), Aquatic Animal Health Management (microbiology, pathology, and disease diagnostics), Aquatic Environment Management (limnology, oceanography, aquatic pollution), Fish Processing Technology (seafood biochemistry, microbiology, freezing, canning, and value addition), Fisheries Engineering (fishing gear design, navigation, and aquaculture farm engineering), and Fisheries Extension & Economics.

Practical training is central to the curriculum, utilizing university fish farms, shrimp hatcheries, research vessels, and processing plants. Under the final-year Student READY scheme, students complete Rural Fisheries Work Experience (RFWE) and an intensive in-plant internship with commercial processing plants or hatcheries.

highlights.label: Practical modules
highlights.value: Student READY: RFWE & in-plant commercial seafood training

who_should_apply: Class 12 science students with Biology, Chemistry, and Physics interested in marine science, aquatic ecosystems, and aquaculture technology
Those seeking rewarding careers in the booming commercial shrimp farming, pearl culture, fish hatchery, and seafood export industries
Applicants aspiring to government technical roles as Fisheries Development Officers or research scientists in national fisheries institutes (CMFRI, CIFA, CIFT)
Candidates enthusiastic about coastal community development, fishing gear design, and marine conservation

curriculum.heading: How the four years are organised
curriculum.intro: The B.F.Sc. curriculum is structured according to ICAR Deans Committee standards across eight academic semesters, blending theoretical foundation with coastal and inland field work.

structure.stage: Years 1-2: Foundations of Aquatic Sciences & Aquaculture
structure.focus: Fish taxonomy, anatomy, limnology, soil and water chemistry, aquaculture principles, and fish nutrition.
courses: Principles of aquaculture and freshwater aquaculture
Taxonomy of finfish and shellfish
Anatomy and biology of finfish and shellfish
Soil and water quality management in aquaculture
Limnology and marine biology
Fish nutrition and feed technology
Fish physiology and biochemistry
Fisheries economics and basic statistics

structure.focus: Brackishwater farming, mariculture, aquatic pathology, fish processing, fishing gear design, and navigation.
courses: Brackishwater aquaculture and mariculture
Fish immunology and aquatic microbiology
Fish and shellfish pathology and health management
Fish processing technology and seafood quality assurance
Fish products and value-added byproduct technology
Fishing craft and gear technology
Navigation and seamanship
Fisheries resource assessment and marine biodiversity

structure.focus: Village work experience, enterprise management, and commercial in-plant industrial training.
courses: Rural Fisheries Work Experience (RFWE) with coastal/inland fishers
In-plant training in commercial seafood export processing plants
Experiential Learning Programme (ELP) in fish/shrimp hatchery management
Experiential learning in value-added fish products manufacturing
Seminar, project report, and comprehensive examination

practical_learning.name: Hatchery & Farm Operations
practical_learning.description: Hands-on induced breeding of Indian major carps, catfish, and freshwater prawns; live feed culture (Artemia, rotifers); and nursery pond management.

practical_learning.name: Seafood In-Plant Training
practical_learning.description: Semester placement inside export-oriented processing plants learning HACCP protocols, IQF freezing, canning, and laboratory microbiological testing.

practical_learning.name: Rural Fisheries Work Experience (RFWE)
practical_learning.description: Living among coastal and inland fishing communities to study socioeconomic conditions, fish landing centers, auction dynamics, and co-operative societies.

points: Pass in 10+2 (Senior Secondary) examination with Physics, Chemistry, and Biology from a recognised education board.
Minimum 50% aggregate marks in PCB (40% for SC, ST, PwBD, and designated reserved categories for ICAR quota admissions).
Minimum age of 16 years as of 31 August of the admission year for ICAR quota seats.
State-specific domicile conditions apply for state fisheries university quota admissions.

routes.name: CUET-UG (ICAR All-India Quota)
routes.description: Conducted by NTA with online ICAR seat allotment for all-India quota seats in state fisheries and agricultural universities.

routes.name: State Fisheries / Agricultural University Counselling
routes.description: State-level admission via state CETs (e.g. KEAM in Kerala for KUFOS, TNJFU counselling in Tamil Nadu, AP EAPCET, TS EAMCET, KCET).

exams.name: CUET-UG
exams.note: Required for ICAR all-India quota B.F.Sc. admissions.

exams.name: State Common Entrance Tests (CETs)
exams.note: E.g. KEAM, AP EAPCET, KCET, MHT-CET, TS EAMCET.

steps.title: Check Eligibility
steps.text: Ensure you have Physics, Chemistry, and Biology in 10+2.

steps.title: Appear for Entrance
steps.text: Take CUET-UG (PCB domain) or your state common entrance test.

steps.title: Apply for Counselling
steps.text: Register on the ICAR portal or respective state fisheries university portal.

steps.title: Seat Allotment & Document Verification
steps.text: Verify academic certificates, pay fees, and report to the fisheries college campus.

documents: Entrance exam scorecard and rank card
Domicile certificate for state quota seats

fees.summary: State fisheries universities (e.g. KUFOS, TNJFU, WBUAFS, CoF Mangalore) offer government-subsidised tuition fees ranging between ₹18,000 to ₹45,000 per academic year. In self-financing quotas or private universities, fees range from ₹80,000 to ₹2,20,000 per year. Hostel, vessel training, and mess fees are charged separately.

careers.heading: Career pathways in aquaculture, exports, and administration
careers.intro: India's seafood exports exceed ₹60,000 crore annually, driven by shrimp and fish farming. This generates strong demand for fisheries graduates across commercial hatcheries, seafood export units, feed manufacturing, and government departments.

roles.title: Fisheries Development Officer (FDO)
roles.description: State government fisheries department officer overseeing fish seed production, reservoir leasing, fishermen welfare schemes, and aquaculture subsidies.

roles.title: Aquaculture Farm & Hatchery Manager
roles.description: Manages commercial shrimp or fish breeding, water quality monitoring, bio-security, and larval rearing operations.

roles.title: Quality Control (QC) & HACCP Technologist
roles.description: Inspects seafood quality, cold storage temperatures, microbial compliance, and export documentation in processing plants.

roles.title: Feed Formulation & Sales Specialist
roles.description: Provides technical advisory and distribution services for commercial aquatic feed and probiotics companies.

roles.title: Technical Officer (MPEDA / NFDB)
roles.description: Government technical official supporting seafood export promotion, cold storage development, and coastal aquaculture licensing.

roles.title: Fisheries Field Officer / Bank Technical Officer
roles.description: Assesses loan proposals for fishing boats, cold storage units, fish ponds, and intensive aquaculture projects.

sectors: Seafood Export Processing Plants (US-FDA / EU certified)
Aquaculture Feed Manufacturers (CP Aqua, Avanti Feeds, Godrej Agrovet)
public_sector_routes: State PSC Fisheries Development Officer (FDO) exams
IBPS Specialist Officer (Agricultural Field Officer - AFO - Fisheries eligible)
MPEDA & National Fisheries Development Board (NFDB) recruitments
Export Inspection Council (EIC) technical officer posts
ICAR Fisheries Institutes (CMFRI, CIFA, CIFT, CIBA, CIFE) technical positions
higher_study: M.F.Sc. (Master of Fisheries Science) in Aquaculture, Processing, Aquatic Animal Health, etc.
Ph.D. in Fisheries Science (at ICAR-CIFE Mumbai and state fisheries universities)

skills: Induced fish breeding and larval hatchery management
Water quality testing (pH, dissolved oxygen, ammonia, salinity) and biofloc management
Fish pathogen identification, necropsy, and antimicrobial treatment
HACCP and food safety protocol implementation in seafood processing
Fishing gear design, net construction, and acoustic fish finding
Aquatic feed formulation and nutrient conversion ratio (FCR) calculation

faqs.question: Is B.F.Sc. a 4-year degree?
faqs.answer: Yes. B.F.Sc. is a professional four-year (eight-semester) undergraduate degree recognized by ICAR and UGC, equivalent in professional standing to B.Sc. Agriculture and B.Tech.

faqs.question: Are B.F.Sc. graduates eligible for IBPS AFO banking exams?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Institute of Banking Personnel Selection (IBPS) explicitly lists a 4-year degree in Fisheries Science as an eligible qualification for the post of Agricultural Field Officer (AFO Scale-I).

faqs.question: Which universities in India specialize exclusively in fisheries?
faqs.answer: Kerala University of Fisheries and Ocean Studies (KUFOS, Kochi), Tamil Nadu Dr. J. Jayalalithaa Fisheries University (TNJFU, Nagapattinam), and dedicated fisheries colleges under state agricultural and animal science universities (such as College of Fisheries Mangalore, Ratnagiri, and Pantnagar).

faqs.question: What is the difference between B.Sc. Zoology and B.F.Sc. Fisheries Science?
faqs.answer: B.Sc. Zoology is a general biological science degree covering broad animal biology. B.F.Sc. is a professional applied technology degree covering commercial breeding, fish pathology, seafood industrial processing, navigation, and aquaculture farm engineering.
